comparison: Perfect agreement on the two-state conformational exchange model for ERK2 (C1-C3, C24-C27). Both evaluations affirm the complementary NMR and HDX-MS techniques establish this core finding. Reviewers explicitly state the data support the conclusions and the methods complement each other.

Strong agreement on VTX11e's R-state selectivity (C4-C5, C34, C37, C39, C41-C43). Both evaluations accept these as established findings from prior work by the Ahn group. OpenEval includes C45 (phosphatase inhibition) which peer review does not explicitly address in this result but accepts elsewhere (R11).

Perfect agreement on ATG017 as a critical control experiment (C81-C87). Both evaluations recognize this dissects structural requirements for R-state selection and demonstrates that DFG region changes alone are insufficient, validating the importance of Gly loop movements.

Both address therapeutic implications (C11, C44, C111, C116, C119). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to limited direct evidence beyond MKP3 data. Peer review is SUPPORTED but Reviewer 3 notes 'no detailed rules were identified' as a limitation. Both recognize translational potential while acknowledging speculative aspects.

Strong agreement on the systematic inhibitor survey (C60-C66). Both evaluations affirm the identification of 14 R-state selective inhibitors using complementary HDX-MS and NMR. OpenEval includes C6 which peer review addresses separately. Both praise the thorough, multi-technique approach.

Strong agreement on HDX-MS protection patterns (C55-C59). Both evaluations affirm the differential protection correlating with R-state selection. OpenEval emphasizes C7 (systematic differences) while peer review focuses on methodological complementarity. Both support the data quality and conclusions.

Both address BVD523 as R-state selective (C49, C51, C53-C54). OpenEval focuses specifically on BVD523's characterization. Peer review groups BVD523 with the broader survey of 19 compounds identifying 14 R-state selective inhibitors. Both support these findings.

Both address GDC0994's lack of conformational selectivity. OpenEval focuses on C36, C38, C52 as a control demonstrating specificity. Peer review includes C52 within the broader inhibitor survey (also covering C6, C49-C51, C53-C54). Both support the classification.

Both address NMR probes reporting R-state selection. OpenEval focuses on C68-C70 (specific probes I196, I345 at distal sites). Peer review groups C67-C70 together, emphasizing the complementary nature of NMR with other techniques. Both support the identification of distal conformational reporters.

Strong agreement on crystallographic evidence (C8-C9, C71-C80). Both evaluations affirm the small but systematic structural changes support the conformational selection model. OpenEval provides detailed structural analysis. Peer review emphasizes these changes support the proposed model despite small magnitudes.

Both address hydrogen bonding networks distinguishing R-state inhibitors. OpenEval focuses specifically on C76-C78 (W2 water bridge as structural marker). Peer review groups these claims (C76-C78) with broader crystallographic findings (C8-C9, C71-C75, C79-C80). Both support the structural distinctions.

Both address the mechanistic model synthesizing structural and dynamic data (C10, C87, C90-C91). OpenEval emphasizes integration of multiple data types. Peer review focuses on how chemical variations drive conformational selection. Both support the model as well-rationalized by the data.

Both address MD simulations explaining solution vs. crystallographic differences (C104-C109). OpenEval notes potential sampling limitations but supports the findings. Peer review accepts simulations as demonstrating dynamic differences between states. Both treat computational data as complementary evidence.

Partial overlap on functional validation (C102-C103). OpenEval groups these with MD simulations (C104-C109) addressing solution-crystal discrepancies. Peer review emphasizes methodological rigor and complementarity of techniques. Both support phosphatase inhibition as validating solution measurements.

Both address synthesis of findings into broader conclusions (C88, C100-C101, C117-C118). OpenEval emphasizes ERK2's unique regulatory mechanism. Peer review focuses on how the work explains conformational selection by inhibitors. Both support the main conclusions about ERK2 regulation.

OpenEval addresses unique structural properties of ERK2 activation (C18, C22-C23, C93-C96) emphasizing small magnitude changes requiring solution methods. No corresponding peer review result specifically addresses these background/contextual claims about ERK2's structural uniqueness.

OpenEval addresses broader kinase regulation context (C97-C99) connecting ERK2's mechanism to general kinase allosteric networks. No corresponding peer review result specifically evaluates these comparative/contextual claims about kinase regulation.

OpenEval addresses noncatalytic kinase functions (C112-C115) citing published literature including BVD523-mediated degradation. No corresponding peer review result specifically evaluates these literature-based contextual claims about kinase noncatalytic roles.

OpenEval addresses established ERK biology background (C12-C15) with literature citations establishing clinical relevance. No corresponding peer review result specifically evaluates these general background claims about ERK therapeutic development.

OpenEval addresses background on kinase activation mechanisms (C16-C17, C19-C21) with appropriate literature citations. No corresponding peer review result specifically evaluates these well-established background claims about general kinase biology.

OpenEval addresses nucleotide binding differences between 0P- and 2P-ERK2 (C28-C32) with functional state assignments. No corresponding peer review result specifically evaluates these structural/functional characterization claims from cited studies.

OpenEval addresses previously published inhibitor conformational selection findings (C33, C35, C47-C48, C92) as background context. No corresponding peer review result specifically evaluates these literature-based background claims, though peer review acknowledges this prior work generally.
